01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Thousands of years ago, farming communities grew into settlements.

01.speaker: skeptic
01.text: So somebody planted a crop and accidentally started a civilization?

01.speaker: narrator
01.text: Pretty much. Then the Indian subcontinent started building cities.

02.speaker: historian
02.text: The Harappans built planned cities, traded widely, and standardized weights.

02.speaker: skeptic
02.text: Wait. This was four thousand years ago?

02.speaker: historian
02.text: And they made a drainage system good enough to win an argument with a pyramid.

test.speaker: narrator
test.text: Let's test a map that refuses to sit still.

test.speaker: historian
test.text: Start with a route. Draw the line, then let the places pop in.

test.speaker: skeptic
test.text: Pop in? Please don't make another PowerPoint.

test.speaker: historian
test.text: Relax. The map wiggles, the ink breathes, and the traveler gets lost on purpose.

test.speaker: skeptic
test.text: That is not a navigation system.

test.speaker: narrator
test.text: It is a history video. A little chaos is a feature.

test.speaker: historian
test.text: Watch the water run from the hills to the city.

test.speaker: narrator
test.text: Now we can tune the rhythm before building all thirty sections.

story-test.speaker: narrator
story-test.text: Let's put the mystery on paper: why did this city care about water?

story-test.speaker: skeptic
story-test.text: Because somebody got tired of mud?

story-test.speaker: historian
story-test.text: Start with the map. The river feeds the city, and streets line up like a ruler.

story-test.speaker: narrator
story-test.text: That square is a house, not a tiny palace.

story-test.speaker: skeptic
story-test.text: Those lines under the street are drains?

story-test.speaker: historian
story-test.text: Covered drains, wells, bathrooms. Four thousand years ago, infrastructure had a plan.

story-test.speaker: narrator
story-test.text: When the water moves, the city works. When the paper moves -

story-test.speaker: skeptic
story-test.text: We call it a documentary and pretend that was the plan.

editorial-pilot.speaker: narrator
editorial-pilot.text: This ancient city had better urban planning than my apartment. That is not a compliment to my apartment.

editorial-pilot.speaker: skeptic
editorial-pilot.text: You are comparing a four-thousand-year-old city to your kitchen?

editorial-pilot.speaker: narrator
editorial-pilot.text: I am comparing their streets to the way I park a bicycle. So yes, they are winning.

editorial-pilot.speaker: skeptic
editorial-pilot.text: They had a system, and we have a group chat called maintenance.

editorial-pilot.speaker: narrator
editorial-pilot.text: The Harappans standardized bricks, lined up streets, and built drains under the houses.

editorial-pilot.speaker: skeptic
editorial-pilot.text: This is suspiciously competent. Where is the ancient landlord?

editorial-pilot.speaker: narrator
editorial-pilot.text: The difference is simple: their water had somewhere to go.

editorial-pilot.speaker: skeptic
editorial-pilot.text: Probably hiding behind the world's first excuse: the plumber is on the way.

editorial-pilot.speaker: narrator
editorial-pilot.text: Fine. Civilization wins. My sink still loses.

editorial-pilot.speaker: skeptic
editorial-pilot.text: And that is how a drainage system becomes the most intimidating thing in history.
